S17.01.note: The assistant prefix is a glyph only and does not name the model.
steps: Start the CLI with agi and type any short message, then press Enter.
Look at the answer: its first line starts with the "✦" marker, while your message starts with ">".
Compare with Expected: the marker separates assistant turns from yours, but the answer itself does not name the model; the model name appears only in the grey line under the answer (S17.36).
S17.01.where: agi (start the CLI), then type a message and press Enter; the answer starts after the "✦" marker

labels.text: Thinking

steps: Start agi and type a question that needs a long answer, such as a short paragraph request.
Press Enter and watch the answer area while the reply arrives.
Compare with Expected: text should appear in pieces as it streams, with headings, lists and code formatted (the assistant turn uses the markdown renderer).
S17.02.where: agi, then type a message and press Enter; the answer text fills in below the "Thinking" line

labels.text: Thinking
still working
… working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel

S17.03.note: Whether the indicator is announced to assistive tech was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Start agi and type a message, then press Enter.
Watch the line just above the input: a spinner with "Thinking…" and an elapsed time shows at once.
Wait about 10 seconds before any text arrives: the line adds "still working".
Compare with Expected: the indicator is visible from the start; the code does not show evidence that it is announced to a screen reader, which I did not check.
S17.03.where: agi, then type a message and press Enter; the spinner line reads "Thinking… <seconds>"

S17.04.note: No reasoning-summary or collapsible reasoning disclosure found: searched apps/cli/src/tui for reasoning, thinking, collapse and expand. The closest control is Ctrl-O, which toggles full tool output (see S17.05).

labels.text: showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse

S17.05.note: Status is shown as a glyph, not as a word.
steps: Start agi and type a request that makes the assistant read a file, for example "read the README in this folder", then press Enter.
Look for rows under the answer: each has a glyph, a tool icon, the tool name in bold and a short summary.
Look at the status glyph: a spinner while running, "✔" when complete, "✗" when failed, "⊘" when cancelled.
Press Ctrl-O to show the full output, then Ctrl-O again to collapse it; compare with Expected: name, status and result should be visible.
S17.05.where: agi, then type a request that needs a tool, such as reading a file; tool rows appear under the answer

S17.08.note: No generated-file cards on an answer found. Searched apps/cli/src/tui for generated, download and file cards: only a one-line chip above the input for /image images (tui_app.rs:3304) and a "Files changed this turn" system line (tui_app.rs:8659).

labels.text: /image open to view

S17.10.needs: a signed-in account in Managed Cloud mode (/image is offered only there)
S17.10.note: Inline rendering was not found; download is not offered, only the viewer.
steps: In agi, type /image followed by a short picture description, then press Enter.
Wait for the reply; a row appears above the input with the file name and "/image open to view".
Type /image open and press Enter to open the newest generated image in a viewer.
Compare with Expected: the image should be viewable; the code shows no inline image rendering in the terminal, only the viewer route.
S17.10.where: agi, then type /image with a description and press Enter; then type /image open

labels.text: No assistant response to copy.
Use one of: (nothing) | code | diff

S17.15.needs: a clipboard the terminal can reach
steps: After an answer, type /copy and press Enter.
Read the confirmation in the transcript; it should say the last response was copied with its line count.
Paste into another app (for example a text editor) and check that the whole answer text is there.
Type /copy code or /copy diff to copy the last code block or diff instead.
S17.15.where: agi, then type /copy and press Enter

labels.text: The answer reached this model's maximum length and stopped there.
Ask for a shorter answer, or split the request.

S17.21.needs: a model that can produce a long answer
S17.21.note: The notice printed beside a cut answer suggests asking for a shorter answer; it does not mention /continue.
steps: Ask for a very long answer, for example a long essay, so the answer reaches the model's length limit.
When the notice appears under the answer, type /continue and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new reply should pick up where the last one stopped without repeating it.
S17.21.where: agi, then type /continue and press Enter after an answer that was cut off

labels.text: Nothing to branch, no messages yet.

S17.27.needs: a session that was not started with --no-session-persistence
S17.27.note: Branching forks the whole conversation so far; no code path lets the user pick an earlier answer as the branch point.
steps: Have a conversation with at least one answer in it.
Type /branch, optionally with a name, and press Enter.
Read the confirmation in the transcript and check that the earlier messages are still in the new branch.
Go back to the original conversation and check that it is unchanged.
S17.27.where: agi, then type /branch (or /fork) and press Enter

labels.text: Exported the conversation to
Nothing to export, no messages in session yet.

S17.35.note: Only markdown, json and answer formats exist; no PDF option was found, and a file is written only when a path is given.
steps: After an answer, type /export answer notes.md and press Enter (use /export md <file> or /export json <file> for other formats).
Read the confirmation; it should say the conversation was exported to a path.
Open the file in a text editor and check that it holds the last answer (or the whole conversation for markdown or json).
Type /export with a file name that already exists and check that nothing is overwritten.
S17.35.where: agi, then type /export answer <file name> and press Enter

labels.text: {} in · {} out

steps: Send any message and wait for the answer.
Read the grey line under the answer: it shows the model name, input and output tokens, credits when paid, and the duration.
Compare with Expected: the line names the model that answered and its usage; time and tokens are shown, cost only when it is not covered by a subscription.
S17.36.where: agi, then send a message; read the grey line under the answer

S17.37.note: Code keeps partial output on a cut or failed answer (chat.rs deliver_incomplete and the error path in tui_app.rs), but I did not confirm the incomplete marker is visible in the TUI: the cut-answer notice goes through output::print_warn.

labels.text: The safety system stopped this response.
Rephrase the request and send it again.

S17.38.needs: none (a refusal cannot be produced on demand)
S17.38.note: The refusal is shown as an error row, not as a separate refusal state; I did not run it.
steps: Type a message the model's safety layer would refuse and press Enter (this cannot be triggered on demand).
Look for a red row starting with "✗" under your message, with the refusal sentence.
Read the next step line below it, which tells you to rephrase and send again.
Compare with Expected: the refusal should look different from a normal answer or a generic error.
S17.38.where: agi, then type a message and press Enter; if the provider's safety layer refuses, a red ✗ row appears

labels.text: ⊘ Stopped
… working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel

S17.39.note: No retry offer for a stopped answer was found in the code.
steps: Type a request that gives a long answer and press Enter.
While the answer streams, press Esc or Ctrl-C.
Look for the "⊘ Stopped" line in the transcript, and check that the text that already arrived is still shown with a [stopped] marker in history.
Compare with Expected: the code shows no "try again" offer after stopping; the text you typed in the input box returns only if you had queued messages.
S17.39.where: agi, then type a long request and press Enter; press Esc or Ctrl-C while the answer streams

labels.text: The model returned no response for this turn.
Send it again, or rephrase your message.

S17.40.needs: none (an empty reply cannot be produced on demand)
S17.40.note: The retry is automatic once; the user retries by sending the message again.
steps: Type a message and press Enter (an empty reply cannot be produced on demand).
If the reply is empty, the app sends the turn once more by itself and shows the warning "Sending it once more.".
If the second reply is also empty, look for the red ✗ row "The model returned no response for this turn." with the line "Send it again, or rephrase your message.".
Compare with Expected: an explicit message should appear instead of an empty answer bubble; the retry is automatic, and there is no retry button.
S17.40.where: agi, then type a message and press Enter; if the model returns nothing, a red ✗ row appears
